clauses.clause: 1-101: establishes, effective 1982-10-01, a three-member board appointed by the President to investigate the dispute; members to be disinterested; functions subject to available funds
1-102: board shall conduct a public hearing at which each party appears and testifies
1-103: board shall report on the dispute within 30 days after its creation
1-104: if no settlement within ten days after the report, board shall require the parties to submit final offers within five days
1-105: within 15 days after final offers, board shall report to the President its selection of the most reasonable offer

review.conclusion_reason: Express named revocation by EO 12553 establishes NO operative status at the cutoff and revoked formal status. All five operative sections are covered. February 25, 1986 is the established revocation date; 'not later than' properly avoids claiming that earlier performance or termination has been proved. Reporting deadlines alone do not establish expiry.

verdicts.reason: Held official-printing OCR identifies Executive Order 12386 of October 1, 1982; the page header gives 43939 and the source identifies 47 FR.
Section 1-101 contains the quoted three-member board provision, effective October 1, 1982, with disinterest and available-funds conditions.
Section 1-102 says the board shall conduct a public hearing and each party shall appear and provide testimony.
Section 1-103 requires reporting within 30 days after creation; the quotation is present.
Section 1-104 supplies the ten-day settlement condition and requires final offers within five days.
Section 1-105 requires a report selecting the most reasonable offer within 15 days after submission of final offers.
EO 12553 expressly states that 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked'.
On 51 FR 7242, PDF page 14, the number column expressly lists 12386 between 12385 and 12390. Separated subject text does not obscure the named revocation.
The heading identifies Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986, and the opening printed page is 7237 in volume 51.
The opening sentence says its purpose is 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary'; the quoted continuation is present.
